The board's decision came after three hours of debate, according to the clerk.

Commissioners voted 4-3 to approve the measure, which raises the property tax rate by two cents per $100 of assessed value beginning in July.

“This was not a decision anyone took lightly,” said board chair Renata Okonkwo, who cast the deciding vote.
She added that the county had no realistic alternative.

We looked at every option available to us over the past six months and this was the only one that kept the schools funded.

The budget takes effect July 1 and includes funding for a new elementary school in the Millbrook area, plus raises for county employees.
